title: Mavci control task record
description: CONTROL PLANE. The authoritative half of a task: phase, status, attempts, ceiling. The agent this governs cannot edit it - that is blocker B1.

attempts_total.description: Tries EVER, monotonic, never reset. Distinct from attempts, which counts tries against the CURRENT ceiling and is zeroed by --reset-attempts. Two facts, not two copies of one: the ceiling counter is a retry POLICY, this is a verdict IDENTITY. A verdict is named <id>-attempt-NN.json from THIS, so the name is unique for the life of the task. Naming it from attempts meant that after a reset the next verdict collided with a historical one and overwrote it, destroying precisely the evidence the operator reset past; found when write-once was enforced, and silent before that. OPTIONAL, not required: a required field under additionalProperties:false invalidates every record written before it (0.1.21). Readers default it to attempts, which is exactly right for a task that has never been reset - that is, every task predating this field.

spec_approved.description: LOAD-BEARING, and named as such here because nothing else in this file is. It is the whole difference between the orchestrator EXECUTING an operator decision and the orchestrator MAKING one. --advance-phase refuses unless this is present and its spec_sha256 still matches the spec on disk; free --set-phase, which needs no approval, is operator-only and confirmed. Written ONLY by --approve-spec, which is operator-only and is not reachable by any agent - so the orchestrator can carry a task forward through a decision that was recorded, and cannot record one. THE HASH IS THE POINT: approval is of a specific spec, not of a task. Without it an approval is a permanent unlock and the architect could rewrite the spec afterwards, which is a stale exemption in the shape this repository keeps finding. Fields: at (ISO-8601 UTC), by (who approved - operator), spec_path, spec_sha256.
